title: Cipher and Confession
premise: Cyrus Eastwick, an estate lawyer who has spent years erasing her own past, is hired by a dying client to prove that his estranged wife's murder never happened — or rather, that it hasn't happened yet, according to a will dated three days after her supposed death. Following the will's impossible paper trail, Cyrus uncovers a coastal town complicit in faking the woman's death so she could escape a violent husband, and discovers the 'dead' wife may be the only witness who can clear Cyrus of a crime committed under her old name. When the tide finally gives up what it took — a body that isn't the wife's — Cyrus must choose between preserving her invisibility and testifying to save an innocent man, ending with her confession in open court and the quiet beginning of a life she no longer has to hide.
about_author: Ines Ashgrove spent a decade working in probate offices along the grey English coast, where she collected the strange, half-true stories estates leave behind. She writes mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. A frail client, Edmund Voss, retains Cyrus to prove his wife Maren's murder never occurred, paying triple and dating his instructions before her death. The will he produces bears a notary seal from a town that burned down. Cyrus accepts against instinct; the beat is unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Salt on the File
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. In the drowned town of Greyharbour, records contradict themselves: Maren Voss died twice, once by drowning and once by fire, in different years. A harbor clerk recognizes Cyrus's face but calls her by another name — her old one. The beat: the past tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Cyrus and Detective Inspector Rhys Calloway. Calloway, investigating the original drowning, warns Cyrus off; every witness repeats the same rehearsed grief. Cyrus notices their stories match too perfectly, word for word. The beat: dread sharpening into suspicion that the whole town is lying in unison.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. At low tide, Cyrus finds Maren's coat, dry inside a sea cave, folded with care — not lost, hidden. Inside, a train ticket dated after the death and a note bearing Cyrus's childhood nickname. The beat: vertigo; the case has been waiting for her specifically.

chapters.title: The Price of Disappearing
chapters.summary: POV: Maren (interleaved flashback). Years earlier, Maren bought her death from a fixer who specialized in erasing women, learning that survival costs everything: name, history, the right to be mourned. The beat: empathy and horror — Cyrus sees her own method reflected back at her.

chapters.title: A Client Who Lies Beautifully
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Edmund Voss dies suddenly, leaving Cyrus executor of the impossible will, which names Maren's killer — Edmund himself — and demands she expose him posthumously. His tenderness was theater; the hire was a confession machine. The beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Witness, Wanted
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Cyrus and Calloway. Someone starts burning the town's false records, hunting the living witness. Cyrus realizes Maren is alive, hiding nearby, and that the arsonist knows Cyrus's real identity too. The beat: the hunter becomes evidence; stakes turn personal and lethal.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus finds Maren; between them grows a wary alliance edged with something warmer, each recognizing the other's exile. But testifying would unmake them both. Maren begs her to let the dead stay dead. The beat: love offered at exactly the price of duty.

chapters.title: What the Water Gave Back
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus and Calloway converging. The storm tide yields the cave's true occupant — the fixer, murdered to close accounts — and Cyrus is arrested for a killing committed under her erased name. In a cell, she must decide whether invisibility was ever really living. The beat: climax of exposure; everything hidden surfaces at once.

chapters.title: Cipher No More
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. In court, Cyrus confesses her old name, decodes the will's cipher for the jury, and testifies alongside Maren, whose testimony convicts the arsonist — Edmund's son, protecting the inheritance. Acquitted but unmasked, Cyrus chooses the visible life. Final beat: two survivors walking the tideline, witnessed at last.
